title: The physician's prayer
hookLine: a well-known prayer for physicians is attributed to him, though probably written later

cards: A framed page hangs on the wall of a doctor's office. A prayer in a physician's voice, asking for love of the work and patience with the sick, and at the bottom, a name: Maimonides. It fits.
He was a doctor at court in Cairo. He wrote medical books. Who else would it be?
And yet the trail of that prayer leads somewhere else.

teach.h: A FELLOW HUMAN BEING IN PAIN.
teach.b: The physician's prayer. First, what it asks. In it a doctor asks God for love of the art and of every creature, for a mind clear at the bedside, and to be kept from greed and the hunger for fame.
And it asks that the doctor see in the sick person only a fellow human being in pain. Second, where it comes from.
The prayer isn't found in Maimonides' own writings. It appears in print long after his death, in German, and the scholars who have traced it point to a later physician, often named as Marcus Herz.
Third, what Maimonides did write about healing.

teach.h: HEALING AS RETURNING WHAT WAS LOST.
teach.b: In his commentary on the Mishnah, he treats healing as a duty drawn from the Torah's law of lost property: the command to return what your neighbor has lost, he says, includes helping return a person's lost health.
And the Torah itself names God as healer: "for I am the LORD that healeth thee." Fourth, attributed, not his. The rabbis cared about who said what.

teach.h: SAY IT IN THE NAME OF WHO SAID IT.
teach.b: The Talmud teaches that whoever repeats a saying in the name of the one who said it brings redemption to the world.
So a careful reader can still love this prayer, hang it on the wall and say it, with its true label on it.

how: Jews pray for the sick in synagogue with a blessing called the Mi Sheberach and in the daily Amidah's blessing for healing, and some medical ceremonies read the physician's prayer, often still under Maimonides' name.

practice: Bring to mind one healer, a doctor, a nurse, a therapist, a home aide, the person who sat with someone you love, and see their tired face at the end of a shift.
If you pray, pray for them in your own words, or hold the Torah's words "I am the LORD that healeth thee" for a few breaths. If you don't, simply hold them in mind with gratitude.
